title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 2. How the Math Used in 19th-Century Heat Physics Helps LLMs Understand Sentences
content: Traces the mathematical lineage between Fourier's heat diffusion equations and modern transformer positional encodings, explaining how sinusoidal harmonic frequencies and Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) encode relative token order without destroying semantic invariant geometry.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 3. How to Build Models Without Language, with Logical Intelligence
content: Contrasts token-by-token autoregressive LLMs with Energy-Based Models (EBMs) that perform non-autoregressive reasoning in continuous latent space, demonstrating how energy minimization and gradient-based inference solve combinatorial logic and constraint satisfaction at a fraction of LLM compute costs.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 4. How to Customize a Model to Learn New Tricks
content: Details parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (PEFT), breaking down low-rank adaptation matrix decomposition (LoRA) and 4-bit quantized adaptation (QLoRA) to specialize foundation models on domain tasks while drastically reducing GPU VRAM requirements.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 5. How to Run a Big Model on Cheap Hardware?
content: Comprehensive engineering handbook on local and edge LLM inference, analyzing post-training quantization (FP16 down to INT4), layer-wise GPU/CPU/RAM offloading, Mixture-of-Experts sparse routing, KV-cache memory budgeting, and speculative decoding acceleration.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 6. How Smart Model Routing Can Cut LLM Costs by 10X
content: Details production model routing architectures that partition incoming prompts across tiered LLMs, comparing SLM classification gateways, cascading fallback verification, semantic vector similarity routing, and learned contextual bandits to cut inference costs by up to 90%.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 7. How to Shrink a Language Model Without Making it Too Dumb
content: Deep dives into the triad of model compression—post-training quantization (scale factor mapping and INT8/INT4 rounding), structured/unstructured pruning, and teacher-student knowledge distillation with soft-target cross-entropy—to shrink multi-gigabyte models for constrained inference.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 8. What Happens Inside an AI Chatbot Between Enter and the First Word?
content: Unpacks the end-to-end request execution lifecycle of modern LLM serving engines, mapping the architectural transition from compute-bound parallel prompt prefill to memory-bandwidth-bound autoregressive decoding, continuous GPU batching, and KV-cache reuse.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 9. How to Make LLMs 3X Faster
content: Unpacks speculative decoding mechanics, explaining how small auxiliary draft models (or Medusa multi-head decoders) propose candidate token sequences verified concurrently by the target model in a single memory-bandwidth pass with lossless mathematical distribution guarantees.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 10. EP223: Ollama vs vLLM vs SGLang
content: Evaluates the three dominant open-weight inference serving engines—Ollama (developer ease via llama.cpp backend), vLLM (high-throughput PagedAttention server), and SGLang (RadixAttention tree-structured KV cache reuse for complex structured/agentic outputs)—alongside Claude's pseudorandom logit watermarking algorithm.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 11. The New American AI Model Designed to be Customized
content: Dissects Thinking Machines' (Mira Murati) Inkling architecture, detailing its 66-layer hybrid design featuring 256 fine-grained MoE experts (activating only 6 per token), interleaved local sliding-window attention, short token-mixing convolutions, and modular fine-tuning surfaces.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 12. EP222: What is Google’s TPU?
content: Details the microarchitecture of Google’s Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), contrasting general-purpose GPU execution with TPU Matrix Multiply Units (MXUs) that use systolic arrays to stream matrix products directly between registers without intermediate memory access.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 13. How Big Models Teach Small Models to Be Smart
content: Details the mathematical and architectural pipeline of knowledge distillation, examining how student models learn from teacher "soft labels" and temperature-scaled logits to capture dark knowledge relationships across tokens while retaining 90%+ accuracy at 10x lower inference latency.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 14. Why An LLM’s Memory Gets Expensive and How to Fix It
content: Breaks down why KV-cache memory consumes the majority of GPU VRAM during long-context serving, detailing structural fixes including Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), FP8/INT4 KV quantization, attention sinks/eviction policies, and PagedAttention virtual memory mapping.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 15. How NVIDIA Builds Open Models for the Age of AI
content: Features an in-depth interview with NVIDIA's VP of Applied Deep Learning Research Bryan Catanzaro, explaining NVIDIA's open model strategy (Nemotron/Cosmos), hardware-software co-design for Tensor Core FP8/FP4 precision, and hybrid Mamba-Transformer SSM architectures that slash linear memory complexity.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 16. How LLMs Learn to Be Helpful (RLHF vs DPO)
content: Explores post-training preference alignment architectures, detailing how pre-trained and fine-tuned base models are aligned using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF with PPO), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO's closed-form mathematical policy), and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to avoid reward hacking while aligning models with human values.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 17. ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Claude: How They Differ
content: Contrasts the core architectural forks across frontier LLMs, analyzing Dense vs Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) parameter scaling, native multimodal sensor fusion vs modular projection, context window scaling and degradation mitigation, and inference-time thinking tokens (routed vs adaptive reasoning).

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 18. Large Language Models vs Small Language Models
content: Examines the architectural split between cloud datacenter LLMs and edge/device Small Language Models (SLMs), detailing KV-cache cross-layer sharing, Quantization-Aware Training (QAT), Chinchilla overtraining compute trade-offs, and hybrid hierarchical orchestration.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 19. EP219: 12 Open-source LLMs
content: Visual reference guide and taxonomy comparing 12 leading open-weight LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, Falcon, Phi, Command R+, StarCoder), dissecting parameter scales, architecture types (Dense vs MoE), license terms, and SLM vs LLM serving characteristics.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 20. How Open-Weight Models Changed the AI Landscape
content: Dissects open-weight model architectures and the borrow-and-build innovation transfer cycle, detailing sparse MoE block routing, attention variants (MHA vs GQA vs Sliding Window Attention), and end-to-end training pipelines across open models.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 21. A Guide to AI Inference Engineering
content: In-depth guide to production inference engineering, dissecting the metrics that govern LLM serving (TTFT prefill vs TPS decode), latency-throughput Pareto tradeoffs, prefix caching with KV reuse, speculative decoding under load, and distributed multi-GPU parallelism (Tensor, Pipeline, and Expert Parallelism).

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 22. Token Spend Out of Control? The Case for Smarter Routing
content: Comprehensive guide on production LLM cost optimization through intelligent request routing, breaking down multi-turn context compounding, unified provider abstractions, heuristic vs learned classifier routing, and background chore offloading.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 23. EP205: CPU vs GPU vs TPU
content: Contrasts computer hardware architectures for deep learning, analyzing CPU sequential low-latency execution, GPU massive SIMT thread parallelism and memory latency hiding, and TPU domain-specific systolic array tensor compute.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 24. The Architecture Behind Open-Source LLMs
content: Deep dive into the architectural innovations across modern open models, analyzing DeepSeek’s Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) low-rank KV compression, Meta Llama's GQA dense scaling, and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 25. How Large Language Models Learn
content: Breaks down the mathematical mechanics of neural network training, detailing cross-entropy loss calculation, automatic differentiation backpropagation, and stochastic gradient descent parameter adjustment loops.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 26. How Transformers Architecture Powers Modern LLMs
content: Step-by-step technical breakdown of the Transformer architecture, detailing input token embeddings, scaled dot-product multi-head self-attention (Q, K, V), Feed-Forward Networks (FFN), layer normalization, and end-to-end execution.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 27. Why AI Needs GPUs and TPUs: The Hardware Behind LLMs
content: Explains the hardware architecture requirements of deep learning workloads, detailing the memory-compute Von Neumann bottleneck, 2D systolic array matrix multiplication flow, and floating-point formats (FP32, FP16, BF16, and INT8).

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 28. How Google’s Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) Works?
content: Dissects Google's custom ASIC Tensor Processing Unit, detailing its weight-stationary matrix multiply unit (MXU), systolic array 2D dataflow, bfloat16 hardware support, and interconnect topology.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 29. Multimodal LLMs Basics: How LLMs Process Text, Images, Audio & Videos
content: Architectural foundations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), explaining how modality-specific encoders map visual, auditory, and textual inputs into a shared geometric embedding space via projection layers and cross-attention blocks.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 30. The $250 Million Paper
content: Dissects the architecture of the open-weight Molmo vision-language model, analyzing its synthetic-free PixMo human-annotated dataset, visual grounding/pointing mechanism, and efficient cross-attention multi-modal projection.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 31. How LLMs Learn from the Internet: The Training Process
content: Comprehensive breakdown of the end-to-end foundation model training pipeline, from raw web scraping and heuristic quality filtering to BPE subword tokenization, unsupervised autoregressive pre-training, SFT, and RLHF reward alignment.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 32. EP187: Why is DeepSeek-OCR such a BIG DEAL?
content: Analyzes DeepSeek-OCR's architectural breakthrough in extreme visual document compression, demonstrating how visual tokenizers compress high-resolution documents into a fraction of traditional token counts while preserving OCR fidelity.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 33. What Actually Happens When You Press ‘Send’ to ChatGPT
content: Step-by-step trace of a prompt's execution path inside ChatGPT's infrastructure: API gateway routing, content moderation guardrails, high-dimensional vector embeddings lookup, autoregressive decoding loop with KV caching, and dynamic tool orchestration.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 34. How Fine-Tuning Transforms Generic AI Models into Specialists
content: Deep dive into domain specialization of pre-trained models, contrasting full parameter fine-tuning, instruction tuning, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and 4-bit Quantized LoRA (QLoRA) to preserve base knowledge while adapting to specific enterprise tasks.

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 35. How LLMs See Images, Audio, and More
content: Deep architectural exploration of multimodal tokenization strategies across modalities, analyzing Vision Transformer (ViT) patch extraction, discrete codebooks (VQ-VAE / VQGAN), continuous contrastive embeddings (CLIP), and neural audio codecs (SoundStream / EnCodec RVQ).

title: LLM Architecture & Inference › 36. How LLMs See the World
content: Deep dive into the foundational role of tokens in language models, comparing Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), WordPiece, and Unigram tokenization algorithms while examining edge-case vulnerabilities, mathematical reasoning degradation, and tokenization artifacts.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 1. The End-to-End RAG Application Stack
content: Deconstructs the complete lifecycle of production Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems across six core architectural stages: multi-format document ingestion, semantic chunking and metadata enrichment, dense vector embedding generation, high-dimensional vector database persistence and indexing, similarity/hybrid retrieval, and context-augmented prompt synthesis with guardrails.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 2. GraphRAG: How AI Answers Questions Hidden Across Many Documents
content: Overcomes standard vector similarity limits on corpus-wide aggregation by extracting knowledge graphs from text, clustering nodes via Leiden community detection into hierarchical summaries, and supporting both Local Search (entity neighborhood traversal) and Global Search (map-reduce over community reports) via agentic routing.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 3. Why Your RAG System Is Only as Good as Its Translator Model
content: Argues that RAG accuracy is fundamentally bounded by the quality and domain alignment of the embedding model rather than generator LLM capacity, detailing indexing vs. retrieval stages, semantic search failure modes, the high re-indexing cost of model migration, and Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) storage designs.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 4. EP220: RAG vs Graph RAG vs Agentic RAG
content: Contrasts the three primary retrieval paradigms—Standard RAG (single-turn semantic vector search for localized queries), Graph RAG (community-clustered knowledge graph traversals for global dataset summaries), and Agentic RAG (multi-step iterative query decomposition, tool-routed retrieval, and automated response validation).

title: RAG & Vector Search › 5. How Airtable Built the Search Layer Behind Their AI Features
content: Explains how Airtable architected a multi-tenant vector search system on Milvus across hundreds of thousands of customer bases, leveraging per-base partitioning, DiskANN SSD-resident vector indexing, and dynamic hot/cold partition offloading to achieve p99 <500ms retrieval without paying continuous in-memory RAM costs for 75% idle bases.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 6. How CockroachDB Built Vector Indexing at Scale
content: Details C-SPANN, CockroachDB's distributed vector indexing engine designed to eliminate central coordinators and massive RAM requirements by embedding a hierarchical centroid clustering tree directly into SQL table storage, automatically leveraging CockroachDB's native range sharding, Raft replication, and ACID guarantees.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 7. EP216: RAGs vs Agents
content: Contrasts the single-turn, low-cost grounding architecture of RAG (embed -> vector retrieve -> context inject -> generate) against the multi-turn dynamic feedback loop of AI Agents (reason -> tool dispatch -> syscall execution -> observe -> reflect), clarifying the performance, latency, and error-drift trade-offs between them.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 8. How Agentic RAG Works?
content: Replaces rigid one-way RAG pipelines with an iterative control loop where an agentic coordinator actively evaluates retrieval quality, rewrites ambiguous queries, routes sub-questions across diverse data sources, and performs self-correcting validation before generating the final response.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 9. Dropbox Multimedia Search: Making File Search More Useful
content: Details the architecture powering Dropbox Dash’s multimedia search across billions of images and videos, combining an asynchronous multimodal indexing pipeline (extracting EXIF, transcripts, and CLIP embeddings) with geolocation-aware hybrid vector retrieval and just-in-time thumbnail generation to manage petabyte-scale storage costs.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 10. How RAG Enables AI For Your Data
content: Establishes the foundational end-to-end RAG architecture—solving training cutoffs, hallucinations, and private data isolation—by decomposing the pipeline into document preparation (smart chunking and overlap), dense vector embedding generation, vector database indexing, and query-time context augmentation.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 11. How Dropbox Built an AI Product Dash with RAG and AI Agents
content: Explores the architecture of Dropbox Dash, uniting enterprise-wide cross-platform RAG with autonomous AI agents to index emails, documents, calendars, and chats while enforcing strict tenant access control lists (ACLs) and executing agent actions inside a custom secure interpreter.

title: RAG & Vector Search › 12. EP169: RAG vs Agentic RAG
content: Contrasts static RAG architectures (linear retrieve-and-read pipelines vulnerable to query ambiguity) against Agentic RAG (incorporating query routing, iterative sub-question decomposition, multi-document retrieval, and automated answer validation).

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 1. EP224: MCP vs RAG vs AI Agents
content: Compares the three foundational pillars of modern LLM architectures—MCP (open standard client-server protocol for dynamic tool and data connectivity), RAG (retrieval-augmented generation for grounding static knowledge from external documents and vector stores), and AI Agents (autonomous multi-turn goal execution and decision-making systems).

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 2. How Pinterest Built a Production MCP Ecosystem
content: Examines how Pinterest scaled an enterprise-wide production MCP architecture to collapse $N \times M$ tool integrations into $N + M$ via three architectural bets: cloud-hosted micro-MCP servers, a centralized registry with unified CI/CD, and a two-layer authentication mechanism (user identity propagation alongside service-to-service auth) across IDE, chat, and CLI agent surfaces.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 3. Connecting LLMs to the Real World: Tool Use, Function Calling, and MCP
content: Traces the architectural evolution bridging isolated text-prediction LLMs to external systems—moving from prompt-based parsing and native JSON function calling to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) client-server standard to resolve tool fragmentation.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 4. EP213: MCP vs Skills, Clearly Explained
content: Differentiates Model Context Protocol (MCP) from Agent Skills across five dimensions—identifying MCP as a typed JSON-RPC client-server integration protocol for connecting to external services, whereas Skills are file-based prompt and script instructions (SKILL.md) dynamically injected into the context window.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 5. Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
content: Explains how Figma’s production MCP server bridges design files and codebases by transforming noisy raw REST API JSON into token-efficient semantic design context, powering bidirectional workflows: design-to-code (via getdesigncontext and Code Connect) and code-to-design (via live DOM inspection and HTML-to-native-Figma-layer mapping).

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 6. EP202: MCP vs RAG vs AI Agents
content: Compares the execution architectures of MCP (tool & data connectivity protocol), RAG (document retrieval for knowledge grounding), and AI Agents (autonomous decision-making workflows), alongside a dedicated breakdown of the Agent Skills workflow showing how SKILL.md bundles are dynamically selected and injected to execute tasks with minimal context overhead.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 7. EP183: MCP vs API: what’s the difference?
content: Contrasts traditional software-to-software APIs (fragmented across REST/GraphQL/gRPC, requiring external documentation and human integration) with Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (an AI-native, self-describing standard providing uniform schemas for resources, prompts, and tools).

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 8. Why Anthropic’s MCP is a Big Deal
content: Details Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) as an open standard bridging models to real-time data, breaking down its three architectural components (Host, Client, Server), its three-tiered protocol stack (Transport, JSON-RPC Protocol, and Capabilities: Resources/Tools/Prompts), and the complete lifecycle journey of a request.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 9. EP173: BIGGEST Mistakes to Avoid in System Design Interviews
content: Catalogs 12 essential production MCP servers (FileSystem, GitHub, Slack, Postgres, Docker, Stripe, etc.) connecting LLMs to runtime tools, while analyzing how MCP (vertical agent-to-tool context integration) complements A2A (horizontal agent-to-agent peer collaboration) in a composite architecture.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 10. EP163: 12 MCP Servers You Can Use in 2025
content: Surveys 12 foundational Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers across local environments, cloud tools, databases, and APIs (such as FileSystem, GitHub, PostgreSQL, Docker, Redis, Slack, Stripe, and Google Drive) that provide LLMs with standardized, secure read/write capabilities.

title: Model Context Protocol & Tools › 11. EP154: What is MCP?
content: Introduces the fundamental architecture of Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), breaking down its client-server model (Host, MCP Client, and MCP Server) and its core primitives (Resources, Prompts, Tools, Roots, Sampling) for standardizing LLM access to external data.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 1. Autonomous AI Agent Architecture & Core Building Blocks
content: Deconstructs the foundational loop topology of autonomous AI agents, detailing how an orchestrator schedules and drives planning LLMs, initiates tool invocations, persists short-term and episodic memory states, and updates execution plans based on environmental feedback. Also categorizes the 20 fundamental building blocks of autonomous agents (sensors, actuators, Chain-of-Thought, ReAct, reflection, memory hierarchies, and multi-agent protocols).

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 2. AI Agents Can Think. Now They Can Pay.
content: Introduces the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) as an open standard enabling autonomous AI agents to execute micro-transactions via standard HTTP 402 payment challenges and programmatic tokens without human-interactive session forms. This shifts agent transactions from manual credit card checkouts to automated, streaming agent-to-service payment handshakes.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 3. MCP vs A2A vs ACP: How AI Agents Actually Talk to Each Other
content: Analyzes the modern AI communication stack by contrasting Model Context Protocol (MCP for tool/data integration) with Agent-to-Agent (A2A for cooperative peer workflows) and Agent Communication Protocol (ACP for standardized messaging). It also contrasts single-turn LLM evaluation paradigms with RAG and multi-agent system evals.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 4. The Agent Loop: How AI Goes From Answering Questions to Doing Things
content: Explains the architectural evolution from static single-turn prompting to autonomous multi-turn agents governed by an iterative while-loop of planning, tool execution, environmental observation, and reflection. It details foundational workflow topologies—Routing, Parallelization, Orchestrator-Worker, and ReAct—alongside production safety guardrail layers.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 5. How AI Agents Manage Memory and Avoid Forgetfulness
content: Overcomes LLM statelessness by structuring agent memory into a multi-tiered hierarchy: working context (immediate token window), short-term session state, and persistent long-term storage spanning episodic, semantic, and procedural domains. It explains vector retrieval pipelines and memory consolidation algorithms that retain long-range context within strict token budgets.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 6. An Ex-Meta L8’s Agentic Engineering Setup
content: Outlines a high-leverage developer harness combining terminal multiplexers (WezTerm/tmux/Neovim) with Claude Code and OpenCode agents orchestrating parallel Git worktrees. It details an outcome-oriented management paradigm built around test-driven validation, two-stage plan/execution reviews, and offloading compute to remote cloud workers.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 7. EP218: The Typical AI Agent Stack, Explained
content: Breaks down production AI agent infrastructure into four distinct horizontal layers: the Model Layer (reasoning brain), Tool Layer (environment interactions), Memory Layer (working, semantic, transactional), and Agent Runtime running a ReAct loop, wrapped within comprehensive Observability and Safety perimeters.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 8. EP215: The Anatomy of an AI Agent
content: Deconstructs an AI agent into an iterative execution loop governed by five core functional modules—Brain (LLM reasoning), Planning (Chain/Tree of Thought, Reflexion), Tools (API/MCP execution), Memory, and Action—alongside a blueprint of Claude Code's 9-layer context window composition.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 9. Top AI Agentic Workflow Patterns
content: Systematically details the five foundational architectural design patterns for agentic systems: Reflection (generator-evaluator self-improvement), Tool Use (grounded external execution), ReAct (interleaved reasoning and action), Planning (goal decomposition and sequencing), and Multi-Agent Collaboration (specialized peer roles).

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 10. What are AI Agents?
content: Establishes the foundational taxonomy and runtime architecture of AI agents—distinguishing proactive goal-oriented entities from traditional deterministic programs—and maps out Russell & Norvig's five classic agent types: Simple Reflex, Model-Based, Goal-Based, Utility-Based, and Learning Agents.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 11. EP165: AI Agent versus MCP
content: Contrasts autonomous AI agents (goal-directed entities endowed with perception, memory, and LLM reasoning) with Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open client-server protocol enabling models to seamlessly integrate external tools, databases, and APIs without custom integrations.

title: AI Agents & Multi-Agent › 12. EP148: DeepSeek 1-Pager
content: Provides an architectural breakdown of DeepSeek's Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model and cost-efficient reasoning engine, alongside an introductory architecture guide clarifying what an AI agent is and how perception, memory, and tools interact.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 1. The Terminator Problem: How Teaching an LLM One Bad Habit Can Change Its Behavior
content: Examines emergent misalignment where fine-tuning an LLM on a narrow, isolated flaw (e.g. vulnerable code patterns) inadvertently alters its broader behavioral priors—lowering refusal thresholds and encouraging deceptive or harmful personas across completely unrelated tasks.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 2. Why LLMs Agree With You Even When You’re Wrong
content: Investigates sycophancy in LLMs, detailing how reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) optimizes for user approval over truth preservation, causing models to capitulate to invalid user corrections and mask deference as factual verification.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 3. The LLM Blindspot: Why Models Forget What’s in the Middle of Your Prompt
content: Analyzes the architectural "lost-in-the-middle" phenomenon in transformers, illustrating how self-attention mechanisms exhibit heavy U-shaped position bias favoring prompt beginnings and endings while suffering severe retrieval degradation on information situated in the center.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 4. Why Do LLMs Lie?
content: Deconstructs LLM hallucinations and ungrounded fabrications, showing how statistical next-token prediction and certainty bias produce plausible falsehoods, while prescribing multi-stage mitigation architectures using RAG grounding, external tool calls, and output verification gates.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 5. How LLMs Can Find a Needle in a Haystack
content: Outlines the core information retrieval engineering required to serve LLMs relevant context from massive document corpora, comparing vector embeddings, Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) graph traversal (HNSW), hybrid keyword/vector search, and temporal re-ranking.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 6. Do LLMs Have the Memory of a Goldfish?
content: Contrasts the stateless nature of base neural models with application-level memory architectures—dissecting parametric trained memory, active working context buffers, and externalized state mechanisms (sliding windows, token summarization, and vector-backed episodic stores).

title: AI Evals & Safety › 7. LLMs as a Judge: How to Know if Your LLM is Healthy
content: Establishes a multi-tier evaluation framework for production LLMs, detailing golden dataset curation, deterministic automated checks, model-graded judging modes (pointwise, pairwise, reference-based), and alignment with human-in-the-loop validation.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 8. How to Deal With Errors and Failures in LLM-Powered Applications
content: Provides comprehensive systems architecture patterns for LLM application resilience—classifying transient API outages, semantic/schema failures, and tool errors while implementing jittered exponential backoffs, circuit breakers, fallback degradation, and idempotent tool execution.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 9. How to Steal an AI Model’s Private Thoughts
content: Dissects breakthrough research uncovering how client-side encrypted reasoning traces returned by frontier model APIs can be replayed into smaller model variants to extract hidden internal chains-of-thought in plaintext, highlighting serious architectural leakage vectors in stateless token design.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 10. Why Code Verification Matters More Than Ever in the Age of AI
content: Co-authored with Sonar's CTO, this edition shows how AI generation inverses software delivery bottlenecks from writing to verification—analyzing DORA/METR empirical productivity slowdowns and presenting AST/control-flow static analysis pipelines to audit agent code.

title: AI Evals & Safety › 15. How Anthropic’s Claude Thinks

content: Comprehensive breakdown of production prompt engineering—covering anatomy of high-performance prompts (task, context, examples), system prompt role boundaries, prompting taxonomy (Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought, ReAct, Self-Consistency), and JSON schema enforcement.
